summary: The ML platform landscape in 2026 has consolidated around a handful of cloud-native and multi-cloud solutions, with the global MLOps market reaching $4.39B and projected to hit $89.91B by 2034 at 45.8% CAGR. Cloud deployments account for 51% of the market, with Azure ML, AWS SageMaker, and Databricks Mosaic AI leading enterprise adoption by GigaOm benchmarks. You need a full ML platform when you require reproducible pipelines, model governance, experiment tracking, and scalable deployment infrastructure — if you only need inference, a model API (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini) is sufficient and far simpler.

platforms.name: Azure Machine Learning
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go for compute, storage, and managed endpoints; free tier for workspace and basic features
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-heavy enterprises needing mature MLOps, governance, and deep Azure ecosystem integration

platforms.name: AWS SageMaker
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-use for compute instances, storage, and endpoints; no upfront cost; costs scale quickly at volume
platforms.best_for: AWS-native teams needing breadth of ML tooling, infrastructure control, and tight AWS service integration

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
capabilities: Managed model training on Delta Lake
platforms.pricing: DBU (Databricks Unit) consumption-based pricing; varies by cloud and workload type; enterprise licensing available
platforms.best_for: Data-centric organizations that want unified data engineering, analytics, and ML/AI on a multi-cloud lakehouse

platforms.name: Google Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI)
capabilities: RAG support with Vertex AI Search
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go for compute, predictions, and storage; AutoML pricing per node hour; Gemini API usage billed per token
platforms.best_for: Data-heavy workloads and generative AI use cases, especially teams deeply invested in GCP and Google's Gemini ecosystem

platforms.name: Dataiku
capabilities: Visual and code-based ML workflow builder
platforms.pricing: Enterprise subscription (annual license); pricing not publicly listed; free Dataiku Community edition available
platforms.best_for: Cross-functional teams including non-engineers who need a collaborative, low-code/high-code ML platform with strong governance

platforms.name: DataRobot
platforms.pricing: Enterprise subscription; consumption-based options; pricing not publicly listed
platforms.best_for: Enterprises needing fast AutoML-driven model development with strong governance, compliance, and minimal ML engineering overhead

platforms.name: Domino Data Lab
platforms.pricing: Enterprise subscription; pricing not publicly listed; based on compute usage and seats
platforms.best_for: Large regulated enterprises (pharma, finance) needing reproducibility, auditability, and flexible compute across clouds and on-prem

platforms.name: H2O.ai
capabilities: H2O AutoML (automatic model selection and tuning)
LLM fine-tuning and evaluation (H2O LLM Studio)
platforms.pricing: Open-source H2O-3 is free; Driverless AI and enterprise products are subscription-based; H2O AI Cloud pricing on request
platforms.best_for: Enterprises seeking powerful AutoML with strong explainability, particularly in finance, insurance, and healthcare

platforms.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
capabilities: Integration with all major training frameworks
platforms.pricing: Free tier for individuals; Team plan ~$50/user/month; Enterprise pricing on request
platforms.best_for: ML and research teams needing best-in-class experiment tracking, model debugging, and LLM evaluation across any cloud or framework

platforms.name: MLflow
capabilities: Deployment to REST endpoints, SageMaker, AzureML, Kubernetes
Plugin ecosystem for major ML frameworks
platforms.pricing: Open-source and free; managed via Databricks at DBU cost; MLflow Tracking Server self-hosted is free
platforms.best_for: Teams wanting open-source, framework-agnostic experiment tracking and model lifecycle management embeddable in any stack

platforms.name: Kubeflow
platforms.pricing: Open-source and free; infrastructure and operational costs apply; managed distributions available (e.g., Arrikto)
platforms.best_for: DevOps-mature teams on Kubernetes needing fully open-source, portable MLOps infrastructure with maximum control

platforms.name: Modal
platforms.cloud: Modal Cloud (built on AWS infrastructure, abstracted)
capabilities: Serverless GPU compute for training and inference
platforms.pricing: Usage-based per second of compute; GPU instances billed by the second; free credits for new users; no minimum spend
platforms.best_for: AI engineers and startups needing fast, serverless GPU access for model training and deployment without infrastructure management
